newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives attack Labour economic policy.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives attack Labour economic policy.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservatives on Wednesday accused the opposition Labour Party of planning to run "an economic policy based on contradictory objectives" by having targets for both inflation and growth.
The claim was made by Defence Secretary Michael Portillo at a party news conference held just before Labour was to launch its pre-election campaign.
"The fabric of their (Labour's) economic policy has begun to fall apart," Portillo said.

He said that even Labour's economic advisor Gavyn Davies had admitted it was dangerous to set targets for both economic gowth and low inflation since it could, according to Davies, "seduce policy makers into accepting a rise in inflation pressure for too long".
"Labour has either been dishonest in promising a growth target or it intends to run an economic policy based on contradictory objectives," Portillo said.
He said the Conservatives, by contrast, had been able to achieve growth by concentrating on low inflation.
